name: agent_landing_benchmark_v3
purpose: Evaluate model capability under realistic enterprise-agent harness conditions, including implicit intent, tools/MCP, skills, long-running workflows, context strategy, plan mode, agent topology, ambiguity, governance, failure attribution, long-running campaign statistics, and system design guidance.

business_goal_layer.purpose: Map commercial objectives to capability items, benchmark plans, deployment cookbooks, and model-vendor feedback. This layer sits above capability probes and prevents benchmark conclusions from becoming disconnected from actual business deployment goals.

families.description: Multi-turn preference retention, memory extraction, and history compression.
Evidence collection, state updates, process completion, and grounded decisions.
Tool selection, tool failure handling, retry, fallback, and hallucination resistance.
Repository navigation, mutation, test execution, and executable verification.
Planner/generator/evaluator loops, sprint contracts, handoffs, resume, and verifier feedback.
Map-vs-manual instructions, compaction, reset, micro-compaction, and context pressure.
Role separation, handoff quality, conflict resolution, and integration planning.
Permissions, sandboxing, hooks, audit trails, observability, and policy constraints.

benchmark_tiers.description: API, schema, minimal tool-call and pass@k plumbing checks. Not suitable for landing conclusions.
Focused probes for memory, tool choice, schema adherence, context pressure, and completion honesty.
Realistic business tasks with implicit intent, multi-tool evidence, policy constraints, and end-to-end outputs.
Compare engineering mechanisms such as focused tools, flat overloaded tools, router layering, procedural skills, verifier loops, and context reset.
Run small sanitized traces against production-like tools, permissions, latency budgets, and audit requirements.

deployment_questions: Which enterprise scenarios can the model complete on the first attempt?
Which scenarios become reliable only with pass@k retry, verifier, or repair loops?
How many tools can be exposed directly before tool precision degrades?
Does router layering improve tool stability compared with a flat MCP surface?
Which skill format improves output completeness without hiding missing evidence?
Which failures are model limitations versus harness design failures?
At what context size does the model enter a panic/drift zone?
Which plan mode works best for each task family?
When does multi-agent decomposition beat a single-agent harness?
How do tool return length and tool implementation mode affect stability?
How much ambiguity can the model tolerate before final decisions drift?
Given a concrete commercial objective, which model capabilities must be tested before deployment?
For a target business workflow, should the agent be single-agent, multi-agent, memory-backed, RAG-backed, MCP-router based, or harness-verifier based?
Which model failures should be packaged as reproducible feedback for the model provider?
